items.title: Quasi-finiteness at points over a one-dimensional local ring from conditions at generic points
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f: X to Y locally of finite type and a point y whose local ring is Noetherian of dimension at most one, the lemma gives five alternative hypotheses at generic points of X under which f is quasi-finite at every point of X lying over y (statement lines 3187-3206). The proof first linearises the hypotheses: (4) implies (3) because the quasi-finite locus is open and a dense open of a locally Noetherian scheme contains all generic points of irreducible components, (3) implies (1) by the equivalence between quasi-finiteness at a point and finiteness of the residue field extension there, and (1) implies (2) trivially (proof lines 3209-3218). The non-formal part is the main case: after replacing Y by Spec(O_{Y,y}) and X by one of its irreducible components (proof lines 3221-3237), the author distinguishes whether the generic point of X maps to y or to the other point of Spec(B), and in the second case applies the dimension formula to force the transcendence degree trdeg_{kappa(y)} kappa(x) to vanish, which makes every point of the fibre closed in the fibre (proof lines 3240-3265). The claim is H2: the reduction steps are standard, while the dimension formula computation is the substantive part.
